This appeal is filed by the claimants being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal vide judgment dated 20.01.2020 in MVC No.935/2018 by the learned II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member MACT-11, Ballari.

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
On 06.05.2018, K. Mahadev was traveling in a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-28/F-2062 as a passenger from Hunugund towards Alamatti.

When the bus reached the Hunugund-Alamatti NH 50 road, near Kudalasangama Cross, the driver of the KSRTC bus, drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the back portion of a lorry bearing registration No.KA-01/AG-1325, which was parked by respondent No.3 without any signal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3649 HC-KAR 3.
As a result, the deceased K. Mahadev sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to them on spot.

The claimants, being the legal representatives of the deceased, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, 'the MV Act'), seeking compensation for the death of K.
Mahadev.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
4. Respondent Nos. 1, 2, and 5 have appeared before the Tribunal through their respective counsel.
Respondent Nos.3 and 4 remained unrepresented and were treated as ex-parte before the Tribunal.

5. Respondent Nos.2 and 5 filed the statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the accident occurred due to negligent parking of the lorry by the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-01/AG-1325.
They prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against respondent Nos.2 and Smt. K. Ranjana W/O.

Based on the pleadings of the parties, the tribunal framed the relevant issues.

7. The claimants, to substantiate their case, claimant No.2 was examined as PW1 and marked 27 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.27.
8.

In rebuttal, respondent No.1 driver of bus was examined as RW1, and officer of the insurance company, respondent No. 5, was examined as RW2, with one document marked as Ex.R1.
9.

The tribunal, after assessing the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part and vide judgment dated 20.01.2020 awarded a compensation of Rs.6,46,072 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
The tribunal held respondent Nos.1 to 5 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the appellants/claimants.

10. Respondent Nos.2 and 5, being the contractual obligators of respondent Nos.1, 3, and 4, were directed to NC: 2026:KHC-D:3649 HC-KAR deposit 50% of the total compensation before the tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, the appellants/claimants filed this appeal.
11. The learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side and that the notional income assessed by the tribunal is also low.
Hence, he prayed for enhancement of the compensation.
12. Per contra learned counsel for the respondents submitted that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is just and proper, and do not call for any interference by this Court.
13. It is an undisputed fact that the deceased, K. Mahadev, met with an accident, and suffered injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the bus and lorry.

The charge sheet,
marked as Ex.P.10, confirms that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3649 HC-KAR
Regarding quantum of compensation:
14. The deceased was about 60 years of age at the time of the accident.
It is contended that he was engaged in a goldsmith business and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
However, the appellants/claimants failed to produce evidence to substantiate this income.

15. In the absence of actual income, this Court assessed the notional income at Rs.11,750/- per month, as per the Schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority since the accident is of the year 2018.

Adding 10% for future prospects, in view of the law laid down in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and Others1, it comes to:
